definition: Holding the two main key poses AND the timing between them completely fixed, the choice of WHAT the breakdown pose(s) depict — and, when there is more than one breakdown, the ORDER they occur in — is sufficient on its own to produce entirely different character reads: the source demonstrates this directly with one punch's two keys reinterpreted through six named breakdown choices (a dull 'gym-class' punch, a tight 'seasoned fighter', a wound-up 'power fighter', a head-led 'evasive fighter', a flailing 'hooligan', a measuring 'strategist', and a block-then-strike 'martial artist'), and with a two-breakdown reaction shot whose MEANING changes depending only on whether it goes squash-then-stretch ('registers the thought, then reacts') or stretch-then-squash ('caught off guard, then begins to process').
purpose: Treat the breakdown, not just the key pose, as a primary carrier of character, personality and narrative intent — the source's own framing is 'keys are your main ingredient, breakdowns are the seasoning' — so that identical staging and timing can still serve completely different performances.
visible_effect: The same two start/end drawings, held at the same timing, produce visibly distinct in-between poses, weight distribution, and body-part leadership depending purely on which breakdown is chosen — confirmed directly in this session's frames showing six differently-posed, individually labeled ('Power Fighter', 'Evasive Fighter', 'Strategist Fighter', etc.) breakdown variants of the identical punch keys.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: A viewer attributes an entire personality/fighting-style read to a character from the breakdown alone, even though the keys and overall timing never change — the source's own explicit test case, since nothing else in the shot was varied to produce the different reads.
physical_interpretation: Not a physical claim — a statement about what carries narrative/character information in a keyframed performance.
use_cases: reusing an existing key-pose pair (a generic attack, a generic reaction) across multiple characters or contexts by varying only the breakdown, rather than re-keying from scratch for each personality
deliberately ordering multiple breakdown sub-poses to change WHICH beat reads as the causal trigger (e.g. 'registers first, then reacts' versus 'reacts first, then processes')
diagnosing a generic-feeling action that already has good keys and timing — per this entry, the fix is likely the breakdown's content, not the keys
non_use_cases: a breakdown that is a pure mechanical in-between with no performance intent, which the source itself demonstrates first as the deliberately 'nothing special, nothing unique' baseline case before showing the expressive alternatives
cases where the keys THEMSELVES already fully specify the intended character read, making breakdown variation a smaller, secondary contributor rather than the primary one
interactions: breakdown_placement_shifts_ease_split (W04-31) — a sibling but orthogonal axis: that entry is about WHEN in time a breakdown lands (its bias fraction); this entry is about WHAT the breakdown depicts and, for multiple breakdowns, in what ORDER — a full breakdown-authoring review should consider both

deliberate_lead_choice_for_acting (W02, v18) — directly confirmed and extended: the 'evasive fighter' variant here explicitly uses the HEAD as the leading body part ('wherever his head kind of moves, his body starts to shift along with the head'), against the 'power fighter' variant which uses the whole body/torso to drive the strike — the same deliberate-lead-choice mechanism, now with a concrete cross-character comparison showing lead choice alone changing perceived fighting style

weight_then_strength_formula (W02, v19), the anticipation ladder (W01) — the 'power fighter' variant's explicit use of overshoot specifically 'to show weight' ('I kind of overshot it to show weight') is a direct, named confirmation of overshoot-as-weight-signal from a new, independent source

style_variations.anime: not addressed directly by this source, which is style-agnostic character-animation theory, but the same principle underlies the anime-specific 'deliberate lead choice' and personality-via-breakdown findings elsewhere in this corpus
style_variations.realistic: applies directly and without qualification — the source's examples are deliberately restrained, non-stylized character drawings

cadence_representation: Directly relevant to `authorMotion`'s existing breakdown-authoring step (Slice A: `plan.authorMotion` takes declared phase FRAMES + a PoseSpec per phase, including breakdowns): this entry is direct evidence that the breakdown PoseSpec itself is a primary creative lever, not a mechanical interpolation step, and that a tool defaulting to a 'safe' straight in-between (as `authorMotion` does when not given an explicit breakdown pose) is choosing the source's own deliberately-labeled 'nothing special, nothing unique' baseline case rather than a neutral default. A future starting-recipe or `next_best_actions` suggestion could offer named breakdown VARIANTS (e.g. lead-with-head vs. lead-with-torso) for the same key pair, directly informed by this entry's six-way demonstration.
control_surface: `compile_pose`/`author_motion`'s breakdown PoseSpec argument already lets a caller specify breakdown content directly; nothing currently offers named breakdown-archetype presets (lead-with-X, overshoot-for-weight, etc.) the way this entry's six fighter types demonstrate.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Partially buildable: `analyseChain`'s existing lead/lag measurement can already report WHICH joint leads a breakdown's motion (directly applicable to the head-lead-vs-torso-lead distinction between the 'evasive' and 'power' fighters), and `ai/pose.js measurePose`'s balance/support measurement can report weight distribution at a breakdown frame. Nothing currently frames a COMPARISON across two authored variants of the same key pair as a named 'breakdown character audit', but the underlying measurements already exist per-variant.
generation_or_modification_methods: `author_motion`'s PoseSpec-per-phase mechanism can already author any of the six demonstrated breakdown variants directly; no preset library of named breakdown archetypes exists yet.
failure_modes: treating a breakdown as a purely mechanical in-between and missing the character-encoding opportunity the source demonstrates is available for free (same keys, same timing)
varying keys or timing to chase a different character read when the source's own evidence is that breakdown content alone is sufficient and cheaper
using an inconsistent or arbitrary breakdown choice across a character's different actions, undermining a consistent fighting style/personality the breakdown choices are meant to establish
roblox_considerations: Directly actionable: a single generic attack/reaction animation pair (two keys) could be re-purposed across multiple NPC archetypes or player character customizations by authoring different breakdown poses per archetype, sharing the same start/end keys and timing — a concrete content-reuse strategy for a game with many characters sharing move sets.
performance_implications: None beyond ordinary keyframe authoring cost; potentially a production-cost SAVING since one key pair can serve multiple character variants via breakdown changes alone, rather than needing fully separate key sets per character.
examples: 'think of your main keys, your main poses, as your main ingredient, and the breakdowns as several seasonings you can apply' (video @ 04:00–04:08)

the six-fighter demonstration on one identical punch key pair: 'dull looking punch... nothing special' (baseline, @ 09:00–09:20) versus 'Power Fighter' (@ 09:49–10:27, overshoot 'to show weight', confirmed on-screen label at t≈08:59) versus 'Evasive Fighter' (@ 10:29–11:08, head-led, confirmed on-screen label at t≈10:29) versus 'the hooligan' (@ 11:20–11:46) versus 'the strategist' (@ 11:58–12:30, confirmed on-screen label at t≈12:20) versus a Wing-Chun-inspired block-and-strike (@ 12:32–13:19)

the ordering finding: 'he squashes to register the thought, and then he stretches to make a gasp' versus 'he gasps first, then falls into squash... this gives the idea he was caught off guard, only after the gasp does he begin to have a thought process' (video @ 06:18–06:54)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/wdPbiy-8BRo (Toniko Pantoja, PWOW Workshop) @ 04:00–13:19 — the presenter states the thesis directly and demonstrates it with two extended worked examples (a reaction shot, then six named fighter variants on one punch), all confirmed by on-screen labels in this session's frames (t=05:18 'Power Fighter', t=08:59 'Evasive Fighter'/'Strategist Fighter', t=08:44 the exercise-routine breakdown diagram); experimental until validated
